bugs.error_message: SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: monitor.conditions
bugs.root_cause: Uptime Kuma >=1.23.x enforces NOT NULL on monitor.conditions but uptime-kuma-api library does not pass that field. The failure in ensure_group() propagated into the HTTPRoute CRD discovery except handler, mislogging it as 'HTTPRoute CRD not available' instead of the real cause.
bugs.fix: Monkey-patched UptimeKumaApi._build_monitor_data at module load to inject conditions=[] into its returned dict. Wrapped ensure_group() calls in try/except so failures log with correct context. Also fixed Helm deployment.yaml to skip the ConfigMap /app mount when useCustomImage=true.

bugs.error_message: UptimeKumaApi._build_monitor_data() got an unexpected keyword argument 'conditions'
bugs.root_cause: uptime-kuma-api._build_monitor_data() has a strict parameter signature with no **kwargs — rejects unknown keyword arguments.
bugs.fix: Removed conditions=[] from all explicit add_monitor/edit_monitor kwargs. Monkey-patched _build_monitor_data to pop 'conditions' from incoming kwargs then inject conditions=[] into the returned data dict.

bugs.error_message: Monitor group recreated on every reconcile; sonarr monitor not updated on second reconcile
bugs.root_cause: MonitorType enum values do not compare equal to the plain strings returned by api.get_monitors(). ensure_group() used m.get('type') == MonitorType.GROUP — always False when type is the string 'group'. Same issue in needs_update type checks.
bugs.fix: Added _type_str() helper (returns t.value if enum, else t as-is). Applied to both sides of every type comparison.

bugs.error_message: HTTPRoute monitors created with https:// instead of http://
bugs.root_cause: extract_url_from_resource() for HTTPRoute kind always hardcoded 'https'. HTTPRoute itself has no scheme — determined by the Gateway listener section.
bugs.fix: Inspect spec.parentRefs[].sectionName: if any contains 'https' use https://, otherwise http://.

bugs.error_message: Monitor group created twice when two static monitors share the same group
bugs.root_cause: ensure_group() called api.get_monitors() fresh on every invocation. The WebSocket API does not reflect a newly created group monitor immediately within the same reconcile cycle, so the second call never found the just-created group and created a duplicate.
bugs.fix: Added group_cache dict (created once per reconcile in full_reconcile(), passed through to reconcile_static_monitors() and reconcile_resource()). ensure_group() now checks/writes the cache before hitting the API. Duplicate API calls for the same group name are eliminated entirely.
